items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And he had George Buckhead on clarinet.

ctx.x: If you could run through that, do you remember? Yeah, I heard them.

Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band. And he had Buddy Johnson on trombone at that time. And he had Baby Matthews on drums. And he had George Buckhead on clarinet. And Willie Santiago on the guitar. And Jimmy Brown played the bass. That was Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Superior Band. Now, pardon me. The Superior Band, in that band, I, when I first seen that band, they had, uh, uh, uh, Mac Murray on drums. They had, uh, Cock and Rumble…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: That's right, George Bakke, he's a fine looking man.

ctx.x: Well, at one time, your father said that he was the only good clarinet player? In those days, yeah, in those days.

But later on in years, I mean, around about 1910, when I remember my father of the bands, I knew who was the best clarinet player at that time. Because they had George Bakke and Lores Atillo. Well, they had other clarinet players, but they didn't come up to those guys. I think George was the best. Because any time they played a funeral, I remember they played a funeral on, they had a funeral on St. Anthony, between St. Claude and Lores. And she was a saloon called Delio. These people have a shoe store right here…
On the street they played E flat?
